title: The 10 Best Cordless Portable Band Saws
subtitle: Battery-powered deep-cut and compact band saws for conduit, pipe and strut, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A portable band saw cuts metal cleanly and quietly with almost no sparks, which is why electricians and plumbers carry them. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita, FLEX and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a deep cut capacity, a brushless motor, variable speed and a work light).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Deep Cut Band Saw, 5" Capacity, Tool Only (DCS374B)

avoid.name: RYOBI ONEAND 18V Cordless 2-1/2 in. Compact Band Saw Tool ONLY P590
avoid.flag: Listing's only bullet is about lawn-mower parts
avoid.verdict: A RYOBI band saw listing whose only description is a line about Stens lawn and landscape parts, under a garbled 'ONEAND' title.
reasons: The single product bullet reads 'Stens replacement parts have become a favorite among lawn and landscape professionals', nothing about the saw.
The title brand reads 'RYOBI ONEAND' and the manufacturer part number (1004-431-0017) isn't a RYOBI model number, so it's unclear who is selling it.
We've seen the same Stens bullet on several RYOBI and RIDGID listings; buy RYOBI tools from a listing that describes them.

buyers_guide.q: What's a portable band saw for?
buyers_guide.a: Clean, cool, quiet cuts in metal: conduit, pipe, strut, threaded rod and angle. Cuts are square and burr-free with almost no sparks, unlike a grinder.
Deep-cut saws (4-3/4 to 5 inches) handle large pipe and stock but are heavy. Compact saws (2.5 to 3-3/8 inches) are light enough for one hand and overhead work.
Slower speeds suit hard metals like stainless; faster speeds cut mild steel and conduit quickly. Variable speed lets you match the material.
Pick teeth per inch for the wall thickness: about 14 TPI for thicker stock, 18 to 24 TPI for thin-wall conduit and tubing. Keep three teeth in the material.
Yes, but these saws are designed for metal. For wood curves, use a jigsaw or a stationary band saw.
